overall_reason: Untinted and cool greys carry the inbox, but one avatar is pink #c47a9e while the other two are slate #8c9ab0, and the unread dots add a second, unrelated saturated blue #3d83f6.

score.reason: T-PALETTE-ROLES finds a hue with no role (the pink avatar) and a second chromatic colour beside it; T-NEUTRALS and the text greys are clean.

findings.title: The palette converges to a few roles
findings.evidence: The palette table lists one chromatic fill, #c47a9e (784 px), on the first avatar; 'Jon Park' and 'Ana Ruiz' use #8c9ab0. Maya and Ana are both unread, so the pink does not mark unread.
findings.before: One pink avatar and two slate avatars, with no rule for which gets colour.
findings.after: Avatars in one neutral, or each person's colour drawn from one defined set of identity colours.
findings.why: A colour with no role makes the reader look for a meaning that is not there.

findings.title: One accent across the page, never two (unless a declared full-palette posture)
findings.where: unread dots left of rows 1 and 3, 1440
findings.evidence: The area palette lists #3d83f6 on the 6px unread dots, a saturated blue unrelated to the pink #c47a9e or the slate avatars.
findings.before: Two chromatic hues (pink and bright blue) in a three-row list.
findings.after: One accent for the unread state, with the avatars kept neutral.
findings.why: Two unrelated hues in one small list compete for the same glance.

strengths: The text greys step cleanly: #262628 names, #7a7a7d previews, #9a9a9d times.
The unread state has a shape (the dot) as well as a colour, so it survives grayscale.
not_investigated: T-DARK-MODE: the page renders light; the stylesheet has a dark class theme that the capture did not render, so dark mode is not verified
brand authority: the run has no 00-contract.md, so no brand colours were available for T-COLOUR-SOURCE; sources were traced from the composition itself
contrast and focus: owned by the sweep (A11-001, A11-003) and not restated here
